feedback: If the learner calls the mother the 'offspring' or hesitates over singular/plural: model 'offspring' for the young (one or many) across several sentences; this is settling usage, so do not over-correct.

If 'breed' and 'species' are swapped (a Labrador called a 'species'): clarify that a breed is a variety within a species, and that a trait is a single feature; have them use each in a contrasting sentence.
If a trait is called a 'type' or a 'species': name it a single characteristic/trait and re-separate the three words with examples.

If the learner says the environment changed the coat colour: that change is acquired (caused during life by the surroundings) and is NOT passed on to the puppies. Only coat colour that comes from the parents is inherited, even if it develops as the puppy grows (Dalmatians are born white and get their spots later). Do not let an environment-caused change be labelled inherited.
activities.intendedInsight: Correct use in a live, self-generated description — not a recited definition — shows genuine command, especially sorting traits that came from the parents (inherited) from those gained during life (acquired), and saying clearly whether 'variation' compares individuals of one species or different species.
learnerActions: Tell or write about a dog and its puppies using inherited, acquired, variation, and offspring as you go.
Describe one thing the puppies were born with and one thing an individual picked up during its life, using the right word for each.

Answer follow-up prompts: 'Could the environment change the coat colour at all — and what would you call that?'; 'One puppy learned to sit on command — inherited or acquired, and why?'; 'Use variation in a sentence about just the puppies, not comparing them to another animal'; 'What's the difference between the same breed and the same species?'
activities.title: Describe a dog and its puppies using the words
